climate.overview_html: With Australia and Türkiye pledging a COP31 cover decision that may explicitly acknowledge 1.5°C overshoot (7 October), the diplomatic run-up to Antalya (9–20 November) intensifies just as IPCC-65 opens Monday in Addis Ababa with its AR7 timeline still deadlocked for a sixth consecutive session. NASA and NSIDC confirmed the 2026 Arctic sea ice minimum at 4.6 million km² on 12 September — tied for 10th lowest in the satellite record — marking 20 consecutive years in which every summer minimum ranks among the satellite era’s 20 lowest. A new Nature Geoscience study led by Robert Kopp finds Antarctic ice loss this century is now “very likely” on all pathways, but the highest-ambition emissions cuts still reduce the upper-end 2100 Antarctic sea-level contribution by roughly half versus very-high-emissions trajectories.

items.headline: Australia and Türkiye Agree COP31 Co-Presidency Will Pursue Cover Decision That May Acknowledge 1.5°C Overshoot; Bowen: Focus Is Implementation, Not New Pledges; Text Drafted During Antalya Talks
items.summary: Australia's climate minister Chris Bowen announced at the Fiji Pre-COP on October 7, 2026, that the COP31 co-presidency (Australia and Türkiye) will work toward a presidency-authored cover decision for the Antalya talks. Bowen said the decision could acknowledge that 1.5°C is at risk of being exceeded, while focusing the COP31 agenda on implementation of existing commitments rather than new pledges. A cover decision is drafted by the COP presidency during talks and requires consensus adoption but bypasses line-by-line negotiation. Key disputes remain over whether the text will reference 1.5°C overshoot explicitly and what it will say on fossil fuel phase-out.

items.headline: 2026 Arctic Sea Ice Minimum: 4.6 Million km² on 12 September — Tied 10th Lowest on Record; All 20 Lowest Summer Minima in Satellite Era Occurred in Last 20 Years (2007–2026)
items.summary: NASA and NSIDC announced the 2026 Arctic sea ice minimum on September 12 at approximately 4.6 million km² (1.78 million square miles), tying 2008, 2010 and 2025 for the 10th lowest extent in 47 years of satellite measurements. The 2026 minimum is 1.21 million km² above the 2012 all-time record low. All 20 lowest Arctic summer minima in the satellite record have now occurred during the past 20 years (2007–2026). NSIDC notes no significant long-term trend decline in September minimum extent over the past two decades, with the post-2007 era representing a roughly stable low plateau. Winter maximum was 14.29 million km² on 15 March 2026.

items.headline: Nature Geoscience (Kopp et al.): Antarctic Ice Loss “Very Likely” on All 2100 Emissions Pathways; Paris-Ambition Pathway Reduces Upper-End Antarctic Sea-Level Contribution by ~50% vs. Very High Emissions
items.summary: A Nature Geoscience study led by Rutgers climate scientist Robert Kopp finds Antarctica is 'very likely' to lose ice and contribute to global sea-level rise by 2100 under all studied emissions scenarios. The highest-ambition Paris-consistent pathway carries at least an 89% probability of producing less Antarctic ice loss by century's end than very-high-emissions scenarios. Under very high emissions, the 95th-percentile Antarctic sea-level contribution reaches 25.4 cm by 2100 (median 15.7 cm). The authors argue near-term emissions choices still meaningfully bound long-term Antarctic sea-level risk.

items.headline: IPCC-65 Opens 12 October in Addis Ababa: AR7 Timeline in Deadlock for Sixth Consecutive Session; Trust Fund at Risk by End-2028; COP31 Presidency Schedules 14 October Virtual Consultation
items.summary: The IPCC issued a media advisory on October 9, 2026 confirming its 65th Plenary opens October 12 at the UNECA in Addis Ababa through October 16. The primary agenda remains the AR7 delivery timeline — unresolved across five consecutive sessions. One bloc (EU and small island states) presses for all three WG reports by July–September 2028 to inform the 2028 Global Stocktake; a separate bloc (including some large emerging economies) seeks WG2 and WG3 pushed to mid-2029. A WGI progress report is on the formal agenda. The IPCC Secretariat has warned its trust fund will be exhausted by end-2028 without new contributions.

items.headline: Pacific Resilience Facility Receives ~$15 Million Boost at Nadi Pre-COP From Fiji, Ireland, Netherlands and Denmark; Total Reaches ~$200 Million vs. $500 Million COP31 Target; Leaders Visit Tuvalu
items.summary: Nations including Fiji, Ireland, the Netherlands and Denmark pledged approximately $15 million to the Pacific Resilience Facility (PRF) on October 7, 2026, raising the total to just under $200 million per PRF CEO Finau Soqo. Roughly half of the total has come from Pacific island governments, New Zealand and Australia. The PRF is targeting $500 million after COP31 and $1.5 billion long-term. Delegates were taken to Tuvalu to witness land being created from dredged sand in response to sea-level rise.

items.headline: EU Finalises COP31 Position: Mitigation Work Programme Extended to 2040, 2028 Global Stocktake Mechanism; “No Scope” for New Finance Pledges; Framed Against UNEP Finding 1.5°C Will Be Exceeded Within Years
items.summary: The European Union finalised its COP31 negotiating position on October 6, 2026, calling for extending the Mitigation Work Programme to at least 2040, establishing a mechanism for the 2028 Global Stocktake, and implementing existing commitments rather than making new finance pledges — the draft states there is 'no scope' for additional pledges at COP31. The position directly cites the UNEP Limiting Overshoot report, which concluded 1.5°C will likely be exceeded within a few years and that the most stringent Paris pathways 'are no longer feasible.'

items.headline: Super El Niño Kelvin Waves Raise US West Coast Sea Levels 15–30 cm; Erosion and Flooding Risk From California to Alaska Through February 2027
items.summary: A series of oceanic Kelvin waves tied to the 2026 Super El Niño began striking the US Pacific coast in early October, raising sea levels 15–30 cm along the California shoreline and moving north at approximately 150 miles per day. The surge is expected to continue through February 2027, combining with above-average North Pacific swell and larger-than-average spring tides to create compounded erosion and coastal flooding risk from California to Alaska.

major_events.name: Hurricane Isaias — MADE LANDFALL NEAR DESTIN FL AS CATEGORY 2–3 (~105 MPH) FRIDAY EVENING; NOW POST-TROPICAL; 610,000+ POWER OUTAGES FL/AL; STORM SURGE 6–9 FT; FEDERAL DISASTER DECLARATION
major_events.status: POST-LANDFALL — Isaias weakened to post-tropical status after making landfall near Destin, Florida on the evening of 9 October; the NHC briefly classified Isaias at Category 3 intensity shortly before landfall, though most sources place landfall intensity at approximately 105 mph (Category 2); more than 610,000 customers without power in Florida (379,000) and Alabama (218,000); FEMA federal disaster assistance activated for affected Gulf Coast counties; storm now pushing northeast through the US Southeast as post-tropical
major_events.impact: Storm surge 6–9 feet along the western Florida Panhandle coast; wind gusts exceeding 100 mph near Fort Walton Beach and Milton; 4–8 inches of rainfall near the coast with locally up to 15 inches; widespread tree damage and flooding in Escambia, Santa Rosa and Okaloosa counties (FL) and Mobile and Baldwin counties (AL); continued heavy rain spreading through Georgia and the Carolinas; power restoration expected to take several days to weeks in hardest-hit areas

major_events.name: Typhoon Koguma (JTWC 27W) — VERY STRONG TYPHOON (~120 KT JTWC FORECAST); EXPANDING STORM-FORCE WINDS EAST OF JAPAN; APPROACHING OGASAWARA ISLANDS; RECURVATURE NORTH-NORTHEAST FORECAST NEXT WEEK
major_events.status: ACTIVE — INTENSIFYING — Typhoon Koguma is generating expanding storm-force winds over waters east of Japan as it approaches the Ogasawara archipelago; JTWC’s forecast places peak intensity near 120 kt with central pressure around 955 hPa; the storm is forecast to recurve north-northeastward into the open North Pacific early next week; no typhoon warnings for mainland Japan at this time; the Japan Times noted an unusual October clustering of three western Pacific storms simultaneously
major_events.impact: Growing swells and storm-force seas across the Ogasawara archipelago and waters east of the Japanese main islands; Japanese east-coast ports and east-facing beaches facing increasing swell as Koguma approaches; Super Typhoon status possible if 120-kt peak verifies; track uncertainty substantial beyond day 5

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Haze — ONGOING; SINGAPORE PSI 181 (2026 HIGH, 9 OCTOBER); MALAYSIA SCHOOL CLOSURES ~2 MILLION STUDENTS; 170K+ RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS INDONESIA; 200K+ HA BURNED; CLOUD SEEDING HAMPERED
major_events.status: ONGOING — Singapore’s 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index reached 181 in the central region on Friday — the worst air quality of 2026; Malaysia ordered school closures across Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and multiple states, affecting approximately two million students; Malaysia is pushing for an urgent ASEAN environment ministers’ meeting and stepping up cloud seeding; Bloomberg’s analysis links the season to the 2026 Super El Niño and land clearing; weather modification operations remain limited by insufficient cloud formation for rain-seeding

weather.overview_html: As of Saturday morning 10 October, Hurricane Isaias has weakened to post-tropical after making landfall near Destin, Florida on Friday evening — briefly reaching Category 3 intensity before touching down at approximately 105 mph (Category 2), with 610,000+ customers still without power across the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama and the storm pushing northeast through the US Southeast. In the western Pacific, Typhoon Koguma is expanding storm-force winds east of Japan as it approaches the Ogasawara Islands, with JTWC forecasting a peak near 120 kt before north-northeast recurvature next week. Indonesia’s haze worsened further: Singapore recorded PSI 181 Friday — its worst air quality of 2026 — while Malaysia shut schools across Kuala Lumpur and multiple states, affecting about two million students.

items.source: NBC News / US News / AccuWeather / CBS News / CNN
items.headline: Hurricane Isaias Makes Landfall Near Destin FL Friday Evening — Briefly Cat 3 Offshore, ~105 mph at Landfall; Now Post-Tropical; 610,000+ Power Outages; Storm Surge 6–9 ft; FEMA Disaster Assistance Activated
items.summary: Hurricane Isaias — the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season after a 342-day drought — made landfall near Destin, Florida at approximately 8:30–9:30 PM EDT Friday October 9. The NHC briefly classified Isaias at Category 3 intensity shortly before landfall; most sources place the actual landfall intensity at approximately 105 mph (Category 2) before the storm rapidly weakened. Storm surge of 6–9 feet impacted the western Florida Panhandle coast, with wind gusts exceeding 100 mph near Fort Walton Beach and Milton. Over 610,000 customers lost power (approximately 379,000 in Florida and 218,000 in Alabama). FEMA activated federal disaster assistance for affected Gulf Coast counties. Escambia, Santa Rosa and Okaloosa counties in the Florida Panhandle reported widespread tree damage and flooding. The storm pushed northeast through the US Southeast, weakening to post-tropical status.

items.source: WeatherNews Japan / Zoom Earth / JTWC / Japan Times
items.headline: Typhoon Koguma Approaches Ogasawara Archipelago as Very Strong Typhoon (~120-kt JTWC Forecast); Expanding Storm-Force Winds East of Japan; Recurvature to North-Northeast Forecast Next Week; No Mainland Japan Warnings
items.summary: Typhoon Koguma (JTWC 27W, JMA Typhoon No. 29) is approaching the Ogasawara archipelago as a very strong typhoon, with JTWC forecasting peak intensity near 120 kt and central pressure approximately 955 hPa. The system is generating expanding storm-force winds over waters east of Japan. The forecast track takes Koguma northwestward toward the Ogasawara Islands before recurving north-northeastward into the open North Pacific early next week. No typhoon warnings are in effect for mainland Japan. The Japan Times noted the unusual October clustering of three western Pacific storms simultaneously as a consequence of the warm-SST environment associated with the 2026 Super El Niño.

items.headline: SE Asian Haze Escalates: Singapore PSI 181 (2026 High); Malaysia School Closures Affect ~2 Million Students; 200,000+ ha Burned in Indonesia; 170,000+ Respiratory Infections; Cloud Seeding Hampered
items.summary: Indonesia's 2026 wildfire haze crisis escalated on Friday October 9. Singapore's National Environment Agency recorded a 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index of 181 in the central region — the highest reading of the year — and advised residents to reduce strenuous outdoor activity. Malaysia ordered school closures across Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and multiple states, affecting approximately two million students; Kuala Lumpur's Air Pollutant Index reached about 170. Over 200,000 hectares have burned across six Indonesian provinces, with more than 170,000 respiratory infection cases recorded by Indonesia's Ministry of Health. Malaysia is pushing for an urgent ASEAN environment ministers' meeting. Cloud seeding operations remain limited by insufficient cloud formation. Bloomberg links the season's severity to the 2026 Super El Niño and ongoing land clearing.

items.headline: DANA Cold-Drop Flash Flooding Kills One, Prompts ~90 Rescues in Madrigueras, Eastern Spain; 140 mm Rain in 2 Hours; Four Homes Collapse; Red Alerts Simultaneously in Southern France
items.summary: A DANA (cut-off low) system struck Eastern Spain overnight October 2–3, 2026, dropping more than 140 mm of rain in approximately two hours at Madrigueras, Albacete. The flash flood killed one person, prompted rescue of approximately 90 residents, caused four homes to collapse and submerged more than 150 vehicles. Southern France issued simultaneous red alerts for Hérault and Gard departments.

items.headline: Typhoon Nolo — Only Second Pacific Storm to Cross the International Date Line Since Hurricane Dora (2023); Peak ~155 mph; Now Post-Tropical West of Wake Island; No Land Threats
items.summary: Hurricane Nolo crossed the International Date Line on October 4, 2026 and was reclassified as Typhoon Nolo by JTWC — only the second storm to make this basin-crossing transition since Hurricane Dora in 2023, with a peak intensity of approximately 155 mph (135 kt). The storm subsequently weakened to post-tropical status west of Wake Island and poses no further land threats.

renewables.overview_html: Grenergy closed approximately US$460 million in non-recourse senior financing (BNP Paribas-led, with BBVA, J.P. Morgan, MUFG, Santander and Bank of Nova Scotia) for 446 MW of solar and 1.8 GWh of battery storage across two Chilean platforms — the company’s largest single project financing, bringing its total Chilean non-recourse debt beyond US$2.4 billion. Clearway’s 650 MW Swan Energy Center broke ground in Missouri with a $1.5 billion project financing and a 20-year Google PPA, while Zelestra and EDP added 462 MWh of co-located BESS across two new Spanish solar plants, bringing their Spanish hybridisation partnership above 1 GWh total. Spain confirmed a new September renewable generation record of 50.9%, and Adani’s Khavda BESS expanded to 6.63 GWh — the world’s largest single-location battery outside China.

items.headline: Grenergy Closes ~US$460 Million Non-Recourse Financing for 446 MW Solar and 1.8 GWh Storage in Chile; BNP Paribas-Led Consortium; Algarrobal + Palmas Cluster; Largest Grenergy Project Financing; Chilean Total Exceeds $2.4 Billion
items.summary: Grenergy announced approximately US$460 million in non-recourse senior financing on October 9, 2026, covering two Chilean solar-plus-storage platforms. Algarrobal (fifth phase of the Oasis de Atacama complex): 242 MW solar + 1.5 GWh storage. Palmas cluster: 21 distributed-generation solar projects including hybridisation of six, totalling 204 MW solar + 289 MWh storage. BNP Paribas coordinated and underwrote, with BBVA, J.P. Morgan Chase, MUFG Bank, Santander and The Bank of Nova Scotia participating. The transaction is Grenergy's largest single project financing and brings the company's total Chilean non-recourse debt beyond US$2.4 billion.

items.source: Energy Storage News / SolarQuarter / Renewable Energy Magazine
items.headline: Zelestra and EDP Sign Two New Hybrid Solar-Battery PPAs in Spain: 25 MW/100 MWh at Pedroso (Seville) and 90.45 MW/362 MWh at Valkyria (Castilla La Mancha); Partnership Total Exceeds 1 GWh BESS
items.summary: Zelestra and EDP signed two new hybrid solar-plus-storage PPAs in Spain on October 5–6, 2026, adding a combined 462 MWh of co-located battery storage. The Pedroso plant (Seville) pairs 31 MWdc of solar with a 25 MW/100 MWh BESS; the Valkyria plant (Castilla La Mancha) pairs 150 MWdc of solar with a 90.45 MW/362 MWh BESS — both four-hour systems. Building on prior agreements, the total partnership now exceeds 1 GWh of contracted BESS capacity across four Spanish solar plants.

items.headline: Pivot Energy Closes $173 Million Term Loan for 135 MWdc US Community Solar Portfolio; 51 Projects Across Six States
items.summary: Pivot Energy closed a $173 million term loan facility covering 51 community-scale solar projects with a combined 135 MWdc of capacity across six US states, supporting a portfolio of operating and development-stage community solar subscriptions providing shared access to renewable electricity for residential and commercial customers.

items.headline: Clearway Energy Group Breaks Ground on 650 MW Swan Energy Center in Missouri After Closing $1.5 Billion Financing; 20-Year Google PPA; CIBC/DNB/NAB Consortium; $80M PILOT for Local Schools
items.summary: Clearway Energy Group closed $1.5 billion in project financing and commenced construction on the 650 MW Swan Energy Center in Bates County, Missouri on October 7, 2026. The banking consortium was led by CIBC, DNB Bank and National Australia Bank. The project carries a 20-year PPA with Google and targets commercial operations in 2028. Blattner Energy is the construction partner, with up to 500 jobs at peak. A 30-year PILOT agreement will generate more than $80 million for local schools and county services.

items.headline: GWEC and 50+ Industry Leaders Launch Floating Wind Action Statement in Lisbon; Focus Areas: LCOE Reduction, Finance/Insurance, Supply Chain Scale; First-Mover FIDs Targeted Before 2030
items.summary: The GWEC's Floating Wind Industry Accelerator unveiled its FWIA Action Statement on October 6, 2026 in Lisbon, endorsed by more than 50 developers, manufacturers, investors and insurers. Three focus areas: reducing LCOE for floating wind; expanding access to finance and insurance; and scaling supply chains. The initiative targets first-mover projects reaching FIDs before 2030 in deep-water markets including Japan, Norway, the US West Coast and the Mediterranean.

items.headline: Sumitomo Acquires 49% Stake in Hero Future Energies 500 MW/200 MWh India Solar-Wind-BESS Hybrid in Karnataka; 25-Year SJVN PPA; Commercial Operations March 2027
items.summary: Sumitomo Corporation will acquire a 49% stake in Clean Solar Power (Baniyana) Pvt. Ltd, the Hero Future Energies SPV for a large-scale hybrid project in Karnataka combining approximately 500 MWp of solar and wind with a 200 MWh co-located BESS. The project has a 25-year PPA with government-owned SJVN Limited, with commercial operations planned for March 2027.

items.headline: Spain Renewables Hit 50.9% of Power Mix in September 2026 — New Monthly Record; 52.7% Including Self-Consumption; Driven by Wind and Continued Solar Capacity Additions
items.summary: Spain's electricity grid operator REE confirmed renewable sources accounted for 50.9% of national electricity generation in September 2026 (52.7% including distributed self-consumption), a new monthly renewable share record driven by strong wind output and continued solar capacity additions since Spain crossed the 50 GW solar milestone in February 2026.

items.headline: Adani Green Energy Khavda BESS Expands to 6.63 GWh — World’s Largest Single-Location Battery Outside China; Over 50% of India’s Operational BESS at One Site
items.summary: Adani Green Energy expanded operational BESS capacity at Khavda, Gujarat from 3.55 GWh to 6.63 GWh. Khavda now holds the world's largest operational single-location battery installation outside China, accounting for more than 50% of India's total operational BESS capacity of approximately 12.6 GWh.

science.overview_html: New arXiv preprints from early October extend the week’s rich AI-weather output: DADA (2610.03172) proposes domain-adaptive data assimilation that keeps the forecast model frozen and optimises only initial-state perturbations, enabling pretrained AI models to accept operational initial conditions without ERA5 retraining; Aurora-WRF LoRA adaptation experiments (2610.03747) characterise fine-tuning tradeoffs for regional heavy-rainfall prediction; and a global AI/NWP precipitation evaluation during atmospheric river events (2610.03758) benchmarks both paradigms in extreme moisture-transport regimes. These join the week’s flagship items: Beucler et al.’s review of AI pathways from weather to climate, the Met Office–Turing FastNet, and Xaurora. A Nature Geoscience study on Antarctic ice loss and emissions choices and a PNAS meta-analysis revealing structural disparities in climate tipping point research coverage round out a productive week.

items.headline: Artificial Intelligence Pathways from Weather to Climate (arXiv:2610.09770, Beucler et al.): AI Must Represent External Forcings Explicitly to Bridge Medium-Range and Climate Skill; 13-Author Review Submitted to Science Advances
items.meta: Tom Beucler, David Neelin, Hui Su, Ignacio Lopez-Gomez, Chris Bretherton, Oliver Watt-Meyer, Tapio Schneider, Costa Christopoulos, Will Chapman, Laure Zanna, Aditya Grover, Adam Subel et al. (UNIL/UCLA/Google Research/Caltech/NYU/AI2/UC Boulder) · arXiv:2610.09770 (physics.ao-ph, cs.AI, cs.LG) · Submitted to Science Advances, 7 October 2026
items.summary: Beucler et al. present a comprehensive review of AI emulators and hybrid physics-AI models, identifying the critical gap between weather and climate timescales: AI systems must represent external forcings (greenhouse gases, land-use change, aerosols) explicitly before medium-range forecast gains can extend to climate projection. Two proposed diagnostic tests: (1) whether models treat external forcings explicitly; (2) whether models are robust out-of-distribution, including extremes and counterfactual scenarios. A key finding is that AI models do not appear intrinsically more efficient than GPU-ported dynamical models once architectural complexity is accounted for.

items.headline: FastNet v1.0: Met Office and Turing Institute GNN Embeds Physical Consistency Constraints During Training; Matches or Exceeds Met Office Global Model at Inference Speed; Validated Against Hurricane Ian and Storm Ciarán
items.meta: Met Office / Alan Turing Institute · arXiv:2509.17658 (physics.ao-ph) · Published October 2026
items.summary: FastNet v1.0 is a graph neural network for global medium-range weather prediction that embeds physical consistency constraints during training rather than as post-hoc corrections. The model matches the Met Office's Global Model on most metrics while running tens of thousands of times faster than full physics simulation. Validation against Hurricane Ian (2022) and Storm Ciarán (2023) shows more realistic storm core structures and improved pressure–wind relationships, addressing the sharp-fronts blurring endemic to pure data-driven AI weather models.

items.headline: DADA: Domain-Adaptive Data Assimilation for Global AI Weather Forecasting (arXiv:2610.03172); Forecast Model Kept Frozen; Only Initial-State Perturbations Optimised; Reduced Short-Range Skill Loss Across Deterministic and Probabilistic Forecasts
items.meta: Minseok Seo, Noah Brenowitz, Doyi Kim, Hyesook Lee, Changick Kim · arXiv:2610.03172 (physics.ao-ph, cs.LG) · Submitted 2 October 2026
items.summary: DADA (Domain-Adaptive Data Assimilation) addresses the operational gap between AI weather model training (on ERA5 reanalyses) and deployment (with real-time observation-based analyses). The method keeps the pretrained forecast model frozen and optimises only an initial-state perturbation using a small domain-adaptation dataset, avoiding the cost of full retraining. Authors report reduced short-range forecast skill loss across both deterministic and probabilistic metrics compared to naïve initialisation from operational analyses. The approach provides a practical pathway for deploying pretrained AI weather models with changing operational initial conditions.

items.headline: LoRA Adaptation Strength in Aurora-WRF for Regional Heavy-Rainfall Forecasting (arXiv:2610.03747): Fine-Tuning Tradeoffs Between Global Skill Retention and Regional Precipitation Specialisation
items.summary: This paper studies how LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) rank and learning-rate choices affect forecast quality when fine-tuning Microsoft's Aurora foundation model for a regional heavy-rainfall prediction task using WRF-style regional configurations. The key tradeoff identified is between retention of global-scale skill inherited from pretraining and specialisation for the local heavy-precipitation regime. Results provide practical guidance for practitioners fine-tuning large weather foundation models for specific high-impact weather applications.

items.headline: Global Evaluation of AI and NWP Precipitation Forecasts During Atmospheric River Events (arXiv:2610.03758): Benchmarks Both Paradigms in Extreme Moisture-Transport Regimes; AI Competitive but Shows Regional Biases in AR Corridors
items.summary: This study systematically evaluates AI-based and NWP precipitation forecasts during atmospheric river events globally, a critical high-impact weather regime for water resources. AI forecasts are generally competitive with NWP for AR-associated precipitation at lead times up to 5 days, but show systematic regional biases in specific AR corridors — particularly along the US West Coast and the Iberian Peninsula. The study provides the first global AR-specific precipitation benchmark enabling direct model comparison in an operationally critical extreme-weather context.

items.headline: Nature Geoscience (Kopp et al.): Antarctic Ice Loss “Very Likely” on All 2100 Emissions Pathways; Paris-Ambition Pathway Reduces Upper-End Antarctic SLR Contribution by ~50% vs. Very High Emissions; Window for Mitigation Remains Open
items.meta: Robert Kopp et al. (Rutgers University) · Nature Geoscience · Published October 2026
items.summary: A Nature Geoscience study led by Rutgers climate scientist Robert Kopp finds Antarctica is 'very likely' to lose ice and contribute to global sea-level rise by 2100 under all studied emissions scenarios. However, the highest-ambition Paris-consistent pathway carries at least an 89% probability of producing less Antarctic ice loss than very-high-emissions scenarios by century's end. Under very high emissions, the 95th-percentile Antarctic sea-level contribution reaches 25.4 cm by 2100 (median 15.7 cm). The authors emphasise that the window for meaningful near-term emissions choices to bound future Antarctic sea-level risk remains open despite committed loss.

items.headline: PNAS Meta-Analysis: Greenland Dominates Climate Tipping Point Research (20% of 20,736 Papers); Permafrost Abrupt Thaw Studied in Only 0.7%; Structural Disparity in Scientific Attention Has Policy Implications
items.summary: A PNAS meta-analysis of 20,736 publications on 14 climate tipping elements found that the Greenland ice sheet dominates research attention, appearing in 4,141 papers (20% of the dataset). By contrast, abrupt thaw of permafrost in boreal forests — identified as a major carbon-release risk — appeared in just 139 papers (0.7%). The study identifies a systematic disparity between scientific attention and policy relevance, with several high-risk tipping elements such as permafrost carbon feedback and West African monsoon shifts substantially understudied relative to their potential climate impact.

items.headline: ClimateBench v2.0 (arXiv:2610.04558): Three-Tier Probabilistic Benchmarking Protocol for Climate Models; CRPS Primary Score; Paleoclimate Out-of-Distribution Testing; All Code and Data Public
items.meta: Duncan Watson-Parris et al. · arXiv:2610.04558 (physics.ao-ph, cs.LG) · Submitted 3 October 2026
items.summary: ClimateBench v2.0 establishes a standardised multi-tier evaluation protocol allowing physics-based, data-driven and hybrid climate models to be compared on equal terms. Tier I tests physical credibility via energy conservation. Tier II scores models against post-2015 observations using CRPS as the primary metric. Tier III evaluates out-of-distribution generalisation through paleoclimate simulations covering the Last Interglacial, Last Glacial Maximum and Mid-Holocene. All code, observational data and benchmarks are publicly available.

items.headline: Climate-Driven Atmospheric Angular Momentum Measurably Lengthening Earth’s Day; Projected to Reach 10–18% of Tidal Friction by 2100; Current Rate Unprecedented in 3.6 Million Years
items.summary: New research demonstrates that global warming-driven reorganisation of atmospheric circulation is measurably influencing Earth's rotational dynamics. High-emissions simulations project that by 2100 the atmospheric contribution to day-length increase will reach 10–18% of the long-term tidal friction trend. Under very high emissions, climate-driven day lengthening could reach 2.62 ms per century — potentially approaching the Moon's tidal influence (~2.4 ms/century). The current measured rate of 1.33 ms/century is described as unprecedented in 3.6 million years.

items.source: VU Amsterdam / TU Delft / University of Amsterdam / EMS Annual Meeting 2026
items.headline: Xaurora: Probabilistic Generative Weather Forecasting via Stochastic Interpolants on Aurora Foundation Model; Competitive with DLWP Ensembles at Fraction of Training Cost via LoRA Fine-Tuning
items.meta: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, TU Delft, University of Amsterdam · EMS Annual Meeting 2026 · arXiv preprint (October 2026)
items.summary: Xaurora uses the stochastic interpolant framework to convert Microsoft's Aurora foundation model into a fully generative ensemble forecast system via LoRA fine-tuning. Results are competitive against state-of-the-art NWP ensembles and other data-driven approaches at a fraction of training cost. The principal contribution is a practical pathway for converting any large pre-trained deterministic weather foundation model into a stochastic ensemble system without full retraining.

items.title: Grenergy Closes ~US$460 Million Non-Recourse Senior Financing for 446 MW Solar and 1.8 GWh Storage in Chile; BNP Paribas-Led Consortium; Largest Grenergy Project Financing; Chilean Debt Total Exceeds $2.4 Billion
items.body_html: Grenergy closed approximately US$460 million in non-recourse senior financing on 9 October 2026, covering the Algarrobal platform (fifth phase of Oasis de Atacama: 242 MW solar + 1.5 GWh storage) and the Palmas cluster (21 distributed-generation projects: 204 MW solar + 289 MWh storage) in Chile. BNP Paribas coordinated and underwrote the deal, with BBVA, J.P. Morgan Chase, MUFG Bank, Santander and The Bank of Nova Scotia participating. The transaction is Grenergy’s largest single project financing and brings its total non-recourse Chilean debt beyond US$2.4 billion.

items.title: Reverion Raises $175 Million Series B to Scale Carbon-Negative Solid-Oxide Power Plants Tenfold; Kembara Leads; Allianz, KfW Capital, Aurum Impact and Carbon Equity Co-Invest; New Megafactory in Germany; 74.2% Electrical Efficiency Record
items.body_html: Reverion, a German solid-oxide fuel cell and electrolyzer developer, closed a $175 million Series B on 29 September 2026, led by Kembara (the scale-up fund of Mundi Ventures), with Allianz, KfW Capital, Aurum Impact and Carbon Equity co-investing alongside existing shareholders. The majority of capital goes into a new megafactory in Germany that will scale manufacturing capacity tenfold to 250 MW annually and add up to 800 jobs. Reverion’s solid-oxide systems achieve a world-record 74.2% electrical efficiency, can run in reverse as electrolyzers, and capture biogenic CO2; primary commercial target is data-center dispatchable power. Total raised: US$237 million.

items.title: Clearway Energy Group Closes $1.5 Billion Financing and Breaks Ground on 650 MW Swan Energy Center in Missouri; 20-Year Google PPA; CIBC/DNB/NAB Consortium; $80M PILOT for Local Schools
items.body_html: Clearway Energy Group closed $1.5 billion in project financing for the 650 MW Swan Energy Center in Bates County, Missouri on 7 October 2026, the company’s first utility-scale development project in the state. The banking consortium was led by CIBC, DNB Bank ASA and National Australia Bank. The project has a 20-year PPA with Google. Blattner Energy will construct the project, creating up to 500 jobs at peak, with commercial operations targeted for 2028. A 30-year PILOT agreement will generate more than $80 million for Bates County schools and county services.

items.title: Pivot Energy Closes $173 Million Term Loan for 51-Project, 135 MWdc US Community Solar Portfolio Across Six States
items.body_html: Pivot Energy closed a $173 million term loan facility covering 51 community-scale solar projects with a combined 135 MWdc of capacity across six US states. The financing supports Pivot’s portfolio of operating and development-stage community solar subscriptions that provide shared access to solar electricity for residential and commercial customers without requiring rooftop installations.

items.title: KPI Green Energy Signs Binding Offer to Acquire 507.9 MW Operational Gujarat Wind Portfolio from Alfanar Group for INR 24.1 Billion (~US$288M); Largest Operational Wind M&A in India This Year; Close February 2027
items.body_html: KPI Green Energy signed a binding offer on 5 October 2026 to acquire 507.9 MW of operational wind projects in Gujarat from Saudi-backed Alfanar Group for an enterprise value of approximately INR 24.1 billion (US$288 million). The portfolio comprises Bhuj-1 (301.4 MW, Alfanar Energy) and Bhuj-2 (206.5 MW, Netra Wind) in the Kutch wind corridor. Both projects hold long-term PPAs with SECI with ~21 years of capacity-weighted remaining life. Transaction expected to close February 2027 pending regulatory approvals.

items.title: Enel Green Power Closes Acquisition of 270 MW US Solar Portfolio for $140 Million; Seven Plants Across Virginia, North and South Carolina; ~$20M Annual EBITDA Contribution
items.body_html: Enel Green Power closed the acquisition of seven operational photovoltaic plants in the United States with an aggregate capacity of ~270 MW on 6 October 2026, at a total consideration of approximately $140 million. The portfolio spans Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina, adding an estimated $20 million annually to Enel’s consolidated EBITDA and expanding its US renewable footprint ahead of IRA investment tax credit expirations.

items.title: Inox Green Energy Services Completes INR 550 Crore Payment for Wind World India 4.5 GW O&M Business; Managed Portfolio Expands to 13.3 GWp — India’s Largest Independent Renewables O&M Platform
items.body_html: Inox Green Energy Services completed the INR 550 crore (~US$65M) payment for Wind World India’s (WWIL) 4.5 GW operations and maintenance business on 7 October 2026 via subsidiary Vibhav Energy Private Limited following NCLT approval. The acquired O&M portfolio services Tata Group, ReNew Power, Greenko Group, Apraava Energy and Hindustan Zinc. Combined with the Inox Group’s earlier acquisitions, the platform now manages 13.3 GWp — India’s largest independent renewable O&M operation.
